title: Broken Object Level Authorization on Profile Endpoint (IDOR)
recommendation: Verify the authenticated user's ID matches the requested user_id before returning profile data, instead of only checking that a token is present and valid.

title: Broken Access Control on Admin Endpoint
recommendation: Require a valid admin-role token before returning this endpoint's data. Returning sensitive fields like passwords with no authentication at all is a critical finding.

title: Mass Assignment via Profile Update
recommendation: Apply an explicit allowlist of fields a client is permitted to update (e.g. email, display name) instead of merging the entire request body into the stored record.

title: Server-Side Request Forgery via Webhook Preview
recommendation: Restrict outbound requests to an explicit allowlist of external hosts, block requests to private/internal IP ranges, and never let a client fully control the target URL of a server-side request.

title: NoSQL Injection via Search Filter
recommendation: Never evaluate user-controlled input as code or as part of a query expression. Compare filter values as literal strings, or use a parameterized query API if a real database is introduced.

title: Server-Side Template Injection via Render Endpoint
recommendation: Never splice user input directly into template source. Pass user data in as template *context/data* instead, so it is rendered as a literal value rather than compiled as template syntax.

title: Missing Content-Security-Policy Header
recommendation: Set a Content-Security-Policy header on all responses to reduce the impact of injected scripts and restrict allowed content sources.

title: Missing Strict-Transport-Security Header
recommendation: Set a Strict-Transport-Security header to enforce HTTPS once the application is deployed behind TLS.

title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options Header
recommendation: Set "X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff" on all responses to prevent browsers from MIME-sniffing responses away from their declared content type.

title: Insecure File Upload Accepts Arbitrary File Type
recommendation: Enforce an explicit file extension and content-type allowlist, validate actual file content (magic bytes) rather than trusting the client-supplied filename or Content-Type header, and store uploads outside the web root with randomized, non-attacker-controlled filenames.

title: XML External Entity Injection via XML Parser
recommendation: Disable external entity resolution and external DTD loading in the XML parser configuration (e.g. resolve_entities=False in lxml, or use a hardened parser such as defusedxml), instead of trusting entity declarations found in client-supplied XML.

title: OS Command Injection via System Ping Endpoint
recommendation: Never concatenate user input directly into shell commands or execute subprocesses with shell=True. Use parameterized APIs that accept arguments as a list, and validate inputs against a strict allowlist (e.g. valid IP addresses).

title: Path Traversal via File Download Endpoint
recommendation: Strip directory traversal sequences using secure filename sanitization, resolve canonical absolute paths, and verify the resulting path is strictly confined within the intended root storage directory boundary.

title: Overly Permissive CORS with Dynamic Origin Reflection
recommendation: Avoid dynamically reflecting untrusted Origin headers. Enforce an explicit allowlist of trusted origins, and avoid setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials to true for untrusted or wildcard origins.
